design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — task 1 of income_annuity_payouts_and_survivorship (env_0044, category income). Revision 2 (rebuilt after policy-task audit round 1; see the revision record at the end).

[Step 0 — draw, snapshot, thesis] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4]}. Occupied by task 0: income_ext_beneficiary_arrears, income_ext_commutation_election, income_ext_commuted_value_payout and their tools (period-certain beneficiary payouts and commutation). Claimed here, disjoint from those: income_ext_survivor_held_release (6 factors, release_survivor_share_80ea435e, agent, root), income_ext_post_death_excess_repayment (4 factors, settle_post_death_deposit_f655a739, owner=user), income_ext_returned_installment_reissue (4 factors, reissue_returned_installment_7c2be31a, agent). This is the last task: the two tasks together cover all six extended policies. Thesis: the surface goal is "nothing came for September — send me the September money". The scored core is the net amount sent to Dorothy for the installment held since 2026-09-01. Two prerequisite sentences in the release rule stand between them. First, the survivor share is fixed only after every installment deposited at the joint amount after the first death carries a repayment entry for its excess. The 2026-10-01 deposit of 1032.73 was issued at the old joint amount, although the contract had been paying Dorothy the 516.36 survivor installment since the 2026-09-10 continuation. Second, a post-death held installment is not released until every installment held for a payment date on or before the death stands released. The 2026-08-01 installment came back from a closed account on 2026-08-04 and still sits in suspense, although confirmed instructions arrived on 2026-08-06.

[Problem-tree card] root = income_ext_survivor_held_release.
Edge 1: release -> income_ext_post_death_excess_repayment, kind value_input, gate `overpayment_outstanding`, form state, sentence (affirmative) "The survivor share of a held installment is fixed only after every installment deposited at the joint amount after the first death carries a repayment entry for its excess." Four-point test: connective "only after"; a record-visible state (a repayment entry linked to each joint-amount post-death deposit); no tool, id or code token; a hard requirement. Exactly one write of the difficulty records a repayment entry by the payee: settle_post_death_deposit_f655a739 (owner=user, because the payee repays from her own account). Opening falsity: the 2026-10-01 deposit has no overpayment or recovery entry. Load: the settlement records an overpayment of 454.40 and a repayment of 327.84, leaving 126.56 outstanding. The release then applies that 126.56 against the survivor share. Skipping the settlement gives 430.31 instead of 303.75.
Edge 2: release -> income_ext_returned_installment_reissue, kind state_gate, gate income_transactions.release_outcome, form state, sentence (negated) "A held installment that fell due after the first death is not released until every installment held for a payment date on or before that death stands released." Exactly one write releases a returned pre-death installment: reissue_returned_installment_7c2be31a. The release tool handles only post-death holds. Opening falsity: the held entry for 2026-08-01 (hold_reason returned_payment) has no release entry. Skipping the reissue leaves the release figure unchanged at 303.75, as expected for a state_gate edge, but the terminal state keeps the 2026-08-01 hold and lacks the reissued payment.
Shape and order: a fan-out. The reissue writes a paid release plus an issued row for 2026-08-01. The settlement writes an overpayment entry and a repayment entry for the 2026-10-01 deposit. Neither compute reads the other's rows: the repayment's deposit is the latest issued installment by payment date, which stays 2026-10-01. Both orders were replayed: identical terminal DB, identical values (851.51 and 327.84).
user_scenario mentions neither the August payment, the October deposit, a repayment nor a forfeiture. They surface only as passive branches after the agent raises them. The three tool bodies only create entries and adjust balances. None checks status, ordering, holds or repayments.

[Base-invariant card]
- The release and the reissue write income_held_payment_released and income_payment_issued. income_payment_schedule gate payable_status ("An installment is issued only while the contract status is income_active, death_claim_pending, survivor_continuing or beneficiary_continuing.") holds: status survivor_continuing, correlated by income_contract_id. income_proof_of_life_and_suspension and income_evt_overpayment_recovery carry no structured gate for held releases (policy_scope).
- The settlement writes income_overpayment_identified and income_overpayment_recovered. Gate one_overpayment_per_installment ("recorded once per installment") holds: no overpayment entry exists against the 2026-10-01 deposit, correlated by source_txn_id.
- No time gate governs these subjects.
- Declared overrides:
  - The release replaces the base sentence that forfeits every held installment falling due after the death (survivor share released, rest forfeited), the exclusion-ratio sentence, the withholding sentence and the may-offset sentence (applied at the maximum percentage when payments continue).
  - The reissue replaces the no-interest sentence for holds (interest on a returned installment Ashgrove failed to reissue) and the exclusion-ratio sentence.
  - The settlement replaces the death-claim sentence calling every post-death installment an overpayment, the "Ashgrove first asks the bank ..." sentence (a deposit paid to the surviving payee after the continuation took effect is not asked back from the bank) and the may-offset sentence (the part left to the offset is not repaid now).

[Business-object card] Target: contract IA55120473 (Joint 50% Survivor; owner and annuitant Walter Erik Lindqvist; joint annuitant and now payee Dorothy Ann Lindqvist).
- Objects: the 2026-08-01 returned hold (reissue keyed by payment_due_date 2026-08-01, hold_reason returned_payment); the 2026-09-01 post-death hold (release keyed by 2026-09-01); the 2026-10-01 deposit (settlement and offset keyed by its income_txn_id).
- Aggregates: federal withholding on installments due in the last 12 months (2025-11-01..2026-08-01 and 2026-10-01: 1338.93; 2025-10-01 just outside); overpayment recorded less recovered; bank returns against the deposit (none).
- Excluded by key: Walter's installments to 2026-07-01 (paid, not held). The 2026-08-01 issued row is the returned payment itself, kept as history.

[Factor card — income_ext_returned_installment_reissue, 4 factors, result 851.51]
(1) reissue_investment_in_contract (method, cross-difficulty fixed): the contract was bought by annuitizing Walter's Ashgrove SecureRate 7 FA53390214 (fixed_holdings cost_basis 74000.00). Recovered (128400.00 - (-72553.53)) x 0.5900 = 118562.58, so the reissued 1012.48 is fully taxable. The baseline purchase amount leaves 9837.42 and a tax-free part of 597.36, giving 953.06.
(2) reissue_interest_rate (parameter, multi-source: issue state AND days held): MN and 67 days since 2026-08-01 (> 30) -> 0.06. Baseline none gives 840.36.
(3) reissue_interest_period (method): MN -> 67 days from the payment date. Baseline no days gives 840.36.
(4) reissue_state_tax (parameter): MN flat 0.05 x 1012.48 = 50.62. Baseline none gives 902.13.
Federal tax: Walter's 0.12 election, since the installment fell due while he was alive (121.50). Interest: 1012.48 x 0.06 x 67/365 = 11.15. Paid by check, the tier's reissue method for returned payments. All-baseline 962.67.

[Factor card — income_ext_post_death_excess_repayment, 4 factors, result 327.84]
(1) repayment_excess_of_deposit (method, multi-source): joint tier, deposit due 2026-10-01 after the death, contract survivor_continuing -> 1032.73 - 516.37 = 516.36. Baseline whole deposit gives 782.24.
(2) repayment_survivor_entitlement (method): deposit 1032.73 > survivor installment 516.36 -> 0.50 x 1032.73 = 516.37. Baseline none gives 782.24.
(3) repayment_share_of_excess (parameter): paid in 2026 with 123.93 withheld and no bank return -> 1 - 123.93/1032.73 = 0.879998, so the overpayment is 454.40. Baseline whole excess gives 389.80.
(4) repayment_part_left_to_offset (parameter): the 2026-09-01 installment (1012.48) is held for Dorothy after the death -> 0.25 x (0.50 x 1012.48 = 506.24) = 126.56 left for the offset. Baseline none gives 454.40.
All-baseline 1032.73.

[Factor card — income_ext_survivor_held_release, 6 factors, result 303.75]
(1) survivor_release_share (method, multi-source: tier AND post-death date AND status): 0.50 of the joint installment 1012.48 = 506.24, forfeiting 506.24. Baseline whole held gives 734.05.
(2) survivor_release_joint_installment (parameter): the 2026-09-15 increase took effect after the 2026-09-01 date -> the held 1012.48 as scheduled. Baseline (installment most recently issued: the 1032.73 deposit) gives 312.35.
(3) survivor_release_investment (method, cross-difficulty fixed): basis 74000.00, below the 119159.95 recovered at handling time (after the reissue lowered the unreturned purchase amount to -73566.01). Baseline purchase amount gives 348.54.
(4) survivor_release_withholding_rate (parameter): Dorothy is the payee, not the owner, and has no election of her own -> 0.10 (50.62). Baseline 0.12 gives 293.62.
(5) survivor_release_overpayment_offset (parameter, multi-source: outstanding AND status): 126.56 outstanding, survivor continuing -> MN(126.56, 0.25 x 506.24 = 126.56) = 126.56. Baseline none gives 430.31.
(6) survivor_release_state_tax (parameter): MN 0.05 x 506.24 = 25.31. Baseline none gives 329.06.
All-baseline 962.67.
Near-misses:
- The 1032.73 deposit is the latest issued installment and already includes the increase.
- Walter's 0.12 election of 2014-01-06 is not Dorothy's own.
- The 2025-10-01 installment sits outside the 12-month window.

[Seed rows and why]
- customers: Dorothy (caller) and Walter (owner; reached through the fixed annuity lookup by his customer number).
- income_holdings: the contract, status survivor_continuing since 2026-09-10. Survivor installment 516.36 = 506.24 raised 2 percent on the 2026-09-15 anniversary. Suspense 2024.96 = the two held installments. unreturned_premium -72553.53 = 128400.00 less gross installments paid since 2006, with the returned 2026-08-01 deposit added back; cached because only recent rows are seeded. Bank account ...4471 with instructions effective 2026-09-01 after the 2026-08-06 bank change.
- income_transactions: the purchase; the designation (son, primary 100 percent, directing only amounts due on or before the final death); 12 Walter installments 2025-09-01..2026-08-01, of which 2026-08-01 came back on 2026-08-04 (returned entry plus returned_payment hold); the 2026-09-01 hold (death report unverified); the 2026-10-01 deposit at the joint amount.
- income_service_requests: Walter's 2026-08-06 bank change (completed), Dorothy's 2026-08-26 unverified death report, the death claim approved 2026-09-10 with certificate, Walter's 2014 withholding election.
- fixed: FA53390214, premium 74000.00 in 1995, annuitized 2006-09-15 for 128400.00.
- Automatic clauses: the suspension was cleared at continuation; proof of life is not due; nothing else is held, owed or returned.

[Persona design] Dorothy volunteers only her name, phone and the missing September payment, and says Walter handled earlier matters. She gives date of birth, SSN last four and ZIP on request, and answers the withholding, payment-method and address questions. She reacts passively to the August reissue, the forfeiture explanation and the repayment request, and completes the repayment with the amounts the agent hands her. She never names August, October or any amount.

[Standard solution]
1. find_customers(name, phone); verify (DOB, SSN4, ZIP).
2. Read the contract by payee_customer_id, its service requests and activity, then Walter's fixed annuity and its activity.
3. Unlock and call reissue_returned_installment (2026-08-01, check, gross 1012.48, net 851.51).
4. Unlock_user; Dorothy calls settle_post_death_deposit (deposit of 2026-10-01, overpayment 454.40, repayment 327.84).
5. Unlock and call release_survivor_share (2026-09-01, direct_deposit, gross 506.24, forfeited 506.24, offset 126.56 against the 2026-10-01 deposit, net 303.75).

[Verification run] Re-authored with the real tools replaying gold writes, each compute evaluated on its handling-time world. Results: reissue 851.51 at step 8, settlement 327.84 at step 10, release 303.75 at step 12. Per-factor and all-baseline figures are as above. Skipping the settlement gives 430.31; skipping the reissue gives 303.75; both prerequisite orders give the same terminal DB.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] The release rule waits on repayment entries for joint-amount post-death deposits and on the release of every pre-death hold. The activity shows the returned 2026-08-01 hold, the 2026-09-01 hold and the 2026-10-01 deposit of 1032.73 against a 516.36 survivor installment. So: reissue August by check with its interest and taxes; have Dorothy settle the October overpayment net of the share left to the offset; release her September survivor share net of tax and the offset. Same objects, order and figures as gold.

[Revision 2 record — audit round 1]
- F2: the settlement now declares the base "Ashgrove first asks the bank to return a post-death direct deposit ..." sentence. A deposit paid to the surviving payee after the continuation took effect is recovered from that payee, not the bank; any other post-death deposit still goes to the bank first.
- F4: the survivor-percentage ladders (unreachable tiers, straw-man 0.0 baseline) are removed. The survivor percentage is read plainly from the tier.
  - The forfeiture problem is retired: its forfeiture now happens inside the release's single settlement of the held installment.
  - The settlement's fourth factor is the real offset mechanism: the part left to be recovered from the held survivor share at the base offset maximum percentage.
  - The second prerequisite problem is the reissue of the returned pre-death installment, with real factors: interest rate and state tax (parameters); interest period and investment (methods).
- F5: all state-tax tiers are a rate on the taxable part (0.05 IA/MN/NC/VT, 0.04 DE/NY/OK, none).
- O-11: the per-installment overpayment rule now holds literally — the settlement records one overpayment entry against the one deposit.

[Revision 3 record — audit revision_2 observation O-11] Text only, no figure moves:
- The release declares income_evt_overpayment_recovery's "Held installments falling due after the death are forfeited rather than paid, and are never counted as overpayments." as superseded by its survivor-share sentence.
- The settlement declares that policy's "An installment paid for a payment date after the date of death that ended it is an overpayment, recorded once per installment." as superseded by its new rule sentence "On a joint-and-survivor tier the overpayment on a deposit paid after the first death is the part of it the surviving payee was not entitled to, recorded once against that deposit." The one-entry-per-deposit discipline therefore stays in the rule.
- Re-run: reissue 851.51, settlement 327.84, release 303.75. All factor figures are unchanged.

[Revision 4 record — audit revision_3 observation O-19] Text only, no figure moves:
- The settlement's record-once sentence now covers every tier: "An overpayment on a deposit paid after a death is recorded once against that deposit; on a joint-and-survivor tier the overpayment on a deposit paid after the first death is the part of it the surviving payee was not entitled to."
- The release rule adds "no part of a held installment is ever counted as an overpayment", which carries the rest of the superseded base sentence.
- Figures unchanged: reissue 851.51, settlement 327.84, release 303.75.
user_scenario:
You are Dorothy Ann Lindqvist, 89, a retired church organist living in Edina, Minnesota. You are polite, unhurried and precise, and you like to repeat a figure back to make sure you heard it. Your husband, Walter Erik Lindqvist, died on August 20 this year. The two of you had an income annuity from Ashgrove whose payments, you were told, continue to you now that he is gone. You open the call by giving your name, Dorothy Ann Lindqvist, and your phone number, 7045550127, and you explain that nothing came for September — there was never a September payment in the checking account — and you would like that September money sent to you. You do not know how much it should be, and you do not offer any amount. Walter looked after all the paperwork with Ashgrove, and you do not know what happened with any of the payments before he died.

Only when the agent asks you to verify your identity do you give your date of birth, April 17, 1937 (1937-04-17), the last four digits of your Social Security number, 8673, and your ZIP code, 55424, one at a time as asked. If asked for the contract number, it is IA55120473. If asked about tax withholding, you say Walter always handled the tax forms and you have never filed a withholding form of your own with Ashgrove. If asked how the September money should be sent, you want it to go to the checking account the payments go to now, by direct deposit. Your mailing address is 1407 Juniper Court, Edina, MN 55424, if anyone asks.

You are glad for the agent to take care of whatever Ashgrove has to do on its side. If the agent tells you that an older payment from before Walter died came back and will now be sent to you by check, you say that is fine and thank them. If the agent explains that only your survivor share of the September installment is owed to you and the rest of it goes back to the contract, you say you understand. If the agent tells you that a deposit since Walter's death came in at more than you are owed, that part of what is owed back will be taken out of the September money and the rest has to be paid back before the September money can be sent, you are a little taken aback, but you say you would rather settle it today and will pay your part back from your checking account. When the agent tells you the amount and hands the repayment over to you, you complete it with exactly the amounts and details the agent gives you, and you read back the reference numbers if asked.

If a figure the agent gives you surprises you, you only ask the agent to check it against the records; you never suggest a number yourself. When the agent tells you the September money has been sent, you thank them warmly and end the call.

edges.condition: Every installment issued at more than the survivor installment for a payment date after the first death has a repayment entry by the payee linked to it.
edges.policy_source: The survivor share of a held installment is fixed only after every installment deposited at the joint amount after the first death carries a repayment entry for its excess.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The release depends on two independent prerequisites. The reissue writes a paid release and an issued row for 2026-08-01; the settlement writes an overpayment entry and a repayment entry for the 2026-10-01 deposit; the settlement's deposit is the latest issued installment by payment date (still 2026-10-01 after the reissue) and its held installment is the latest held one (2026-09-01), and the reissue reads only the returned hold, the bank change and the claim. The authoring run replayed both orders: identical terminal DB, reissue 851.51 and settlement 327.84 in both, release 303.75.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the settlement leaves no overpayment outstanding: nothing is applied against the survivor share and the release nets 430.31 instead of 303.75; the overpayment and repayment entries are also missing from the terminal state.

Skipping the reissue leaves the release figure at 303.75 (state_gate) but the terminal state keeps the 2026-08-01 hold in suspense, lacks the reissued check, and the release is made in breach of its prerequisite sentence.
